# Write like people speak

Write product copy in active voice, and read your copy aloud.

## Why

External standard, not learned from the user's feedback. Active voice shows who does what, and conversational copy is easier to read. Reading aloud catches stiff, formal, or unnatural phrasing.

## Prefer

- Use active voice: "@A started 3 threads", not "3 threads were started by @A".
- Use contractions and plain verbs, and start statements with the verb when you can.
- Read the copy aloud, and rewrite anything a person wouldn't say.

## Avoid

- Passive constructions and weak openers such as "there is", or "you can" when it adds nothing.

## Use when

- Writing or reviewing UI copy, notifications, agent messages, and docs.

## Do not use when

- A legal, compliance, or technical reference text requires formal wording.

## Sources

- Microsoft Writing Style Guide: Top 10 tips for style and voice — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/style-guide/top-10-tips-style-voice
- Material Design: Writing (conversational tone and contractions) — https://m1.material.io/style/writing.html
- Grafana Writers' Toolkit: UX writing — https://grafana.com/docs/writers-toolkit/write/style-guide/ux-writing/

## Check

- Does each sentence avoid passive voice, so it's clear who acts?
- Would a person say this sentence aloud, word for word?
